Usage:
  pqax check <file> [--part <name>]   Validate a PQAX file, or the footprint inside a VPAX file.
  pqax info <file> [--part <name>]    Show the format, the collection, the parts, and the rows of each table.
  pqax tables <file> [--sort waste|total|rows|files|name] [--top <n>] [--wide] [--json]
                                      One row per table with its storage, waste, and waste share. See pqax tables --help.
  pqax diff <older> <newer> [--sort total|waste|rows|files|name] [--top <n>] [--json]
                                      The tables and columns added, removed, and kept between two footprints. See pqax diff --help.
  pqax collect --local <folder> --output <file>     Collect a footprint from a folder in the OneLake layout.
  pqax collect --workspace <id> --item <name> --output <file>   Collect from OneLake after a sign-in. See pqax collect --help.
  pqax collect --adls <url> --output <file>         Collect from a container of Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 after a sign-in.
  pqax --version                      Show the version.

A file with the extension .vpax, or any file with --part, is read as a VPAX file that holds the
footprint as a part, Footprint.pqax unless --part names another one.

Exit codes: 0 valid or done, 1 invalid, 2 wrong command line or file that cannot be read.

result.stdout:
Usage:
  pqax tables <file> [--part <name>] [--sort waste|total|rows|files|name] [--top <n>] [--wide] [--json]

One row per table: rows, files, live bytes, the non-live and unreferenced files, the deleted rows, the stale
columns, the waste, and the waste share, as the storage views compute them.

Options:
  --sort waste|total|rows|files|name   The order: the largest first, or by name. Default waste.
  --top <n>                            The first n tables of the order.
  --wide                               Adds the shares of the files under 8 MiB and 128 MiB, the metadata, and the footers.
  --json                               Writes one JSON object with the collection and every measure of each table.
  --part <name>                        The part of a VPAX file that holds the footprint. Default Footprint.pqax.

Exit codes: 0 read, 1 the reader refuses the file, 2 wrong command line or file that cannot be read.

Usage:
  pqax diff <older> <newer> [--part <name>] [--sort total|waste|rows|files|name] [--top <n>] [--json]

Compares two footprints of the same lakehouse: the tables and the columns added, removed, and kept, and the change
of the total size, the waste, the files, and the rows of each table, the largest change first. A table is the same
table when its TableId is, and by its source, namespace, and name when one of the two has none.

Options:
  --sort total|waste|rows|files|name   The order: the largest change first, or by name. Default total.
  --top <n>                            The first n changes of the order.
  --json                               Writes one JSON object with both headers and the tables added, removed, and kept,
                                       with the change of every total and measure.
  --part <name>                        The part of a VPAX file that holds the footprint, for both files. Default Footprint.pqax.

Exit codes: 0 compared, 1 the reader refuses a file, 2 wrong command line or file that cannot be read.

result.stdout:
Usage:
  pqax collect --local <folder> --output <file.pqax> [--item <name.Kind>]... [options]
  pqax collect --workspace <name or id> --item <name.Kind> [--item ...] --output <file.pqax> [identity] [options]
  pqax collect --adls https://<account>.dfs.core.windows.net/<container>[/<folder>] --output <file.pqax> [identity] [options]

--local reads a folder with the OneLake layout: <item>.<Kind>/Tables/[<schema>/]<table>. Without --item, every
lakehouse, warehouse, mirrored database, and SQL database in the folder. --workspace reads OneLake after a sign-in;
an item is named as in OneLake, such as Sales.Lakehouse.
Name the workspace and the items both by name or both by id: OneLake refuses a workspace id with item names.
--adls reads a container of Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 after a sign-in: a folder with _delta_log is a Delta table, a folder
of Parquet files with no subfolder a Parquet table, down to 4 levels below the folder. The identity needs Storage Blob
Data Reader on the container or the account.

Identity, one of these; a secret is read from an environment variable, never from the command line:
  (none), --device-code                         A person, with a device code that the command prints. The default.
  --browser                                     A person, in the browser.
  --client-id <id> --client-secret-env <NAME>   A service principal; the secret is in the variable NAME. Needs --tenant.
  --client-id <id> --client-certificate <file>  A service principal with a PFX or PEM certificate. Needs --tenant.
    [--client-certificate-password-env <NAME>]  The password of the certificate, in the variable NAME.
  --managed-identity [--client-id <id>]         The managed identity: system-assigned, or user-assigned with its client id.
  --azure-cli                                   The account of az login.
  --access-token-env <NAME>                     An access token for https://storage.azure.com, in the variable NAME.
  --env-credential                              AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, and A
[truncated]
